correctness.rationale: For p>=p_a=0.5 sqrt[a(1+a)^n], S_p(w)=sqrt(4p²+w(1-w)^n) remains real for -a<=w<=1. Differentiating the separated Hamilton–Jacobi generating function gives 4 Phi_t Phi_s=(1-ts)^n with admissible nonnegative partial derivatives, hence a calibration upper bound H_n(a)<=F_n(a,p). Under the integral sign, derivative Fp=2Psi; kernel (1-w)^n/[S_p(S_p+2p)] is strictly decreasing p, making Psi strictly increasing and F strictly convex. The source established Psi(a,p_a) sign transition at a_n: boundary p_a below, unique root p*>p_a above. At Psi=0 reflected characteristic contact coordinates match at (sqrt a,-sqrt a), yielding a calibrated attaining causal path. At a=1 any path goes through opposite corner via axis-parallel lines and H=0. As a->1, uniform large-p expansion Psi=log(1/a)-C_a/(8p²)+O(p^-4), C_a=(1+a)^(n+1)/(n+1), gives p*sqrt(1-a)->2^((n-2)/2)/sqrt(n+1), H/sqrt(1-a)->2^((n+2)/2)/sqrt(n+1). Independently computed adaptive quadrature/root of Psi for n=2,3,5 and a=.92,.93,.97, consistent with signs/asymptotic; numeric checks do not replace calibration proof.
